newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan securities issues up 153 pct Jan-April.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan securities issues up 153 pct Jan-April.

text.p: Share and commercial paper issues approved by Venezuela's Securities Commission (CNV) were up 153 percent over the first four months of the year compared with the same period in 1996, CNV President Aida Lamus said.
"We are seeing increases through the injection of fresh capital...That's a sign of confidence," Lamus told reporters in Congress.

Lamus said the CNV had approved share and debt issue worth 203.039 billion bolivars ($413 million) over the first four months of the year, compared with just 80.171 billion ($166 million) between January and April 1996.

Shares accounted for more than half the new issues with 113.639 billion bolivars, up from 38.171 billion in the first four months of 1996. Commercial debt rose to 88.9 billion bolivars from 34 billion bolivars last year, Lamus said.
A small amount of debenture bonds accounted for the remainder of the issues.
